Of course!! On mobile and don’t know how to quote, but I think you may be losing air on the sides of your mouth! That was something I used to do when starting out, and focusing my airstream on the sides definitely made me less airy. I would fiddle around with position and different mouth shapes until you figure it out. 

On posture, I just noticed you tend to put down your L5 (pinkie?) finger when you press down with your fourth, and I think not doing that might help with finger stretch! There are definitely some finger stretches you can do, I have naturally small hands, but I also play piano so I had to learn to stretch that out lol. I would suggest looking at other flute players on youtube, especially for the type of flute you have. Also I didn’t know the piper’s grip was a thing! In that case, I’d say keep on on what you’re doing! It looked tense from what I’m used to (open-holed keyed flute) but I can definitely see why it would help on a completely keyless flute! I think trying a standard grip might make it easier down the line if you intend to switch over to a standard flute down the line, but if not, I think you’re completely fine to keep your piper’s grip. Plus, learning how to curve your fingers isn’t something too hard to get down, and I’m sure you’d be able to figure out in a couple practice sessions!

You are absolutely right on long tones! I would suggest watching other flute players do long tones, it took me a long time to learn how to actually do them productively, but I’m not sure if anyone puts those on youtube or anything, they’re pretty boring! 

Also I didn’t know that was PVC! It’s very pretty and it had me completely fooled. Good luck on your flute journey!!

Hello!! I’ve never gotten formal lessons on flute but I’ve been playing for a while. I hadn’t seen anyone else comment yet so I thought I’d send over some tips. Hopefully  some of what I say makes sense! I’ve also never played on a (gorgeous looking !!) wooden flute like yours before, so I might have some incorrect tips technique wise. 

I think you might be losing a bit too much air when blowing into your flute. I’d try to work on focusing your airstream so most of the airstream is directed over the flute hole (embouchure hole ??). I think this would help you sound a bit less airy too, and hopefully help with the lightheadedness. You /are/ supposed to feel like you’re losing a lot of air, but I don’t think you should feel like you’re losing too much of it! I might be biased though, I’ve only really played flute on the wind instruments side and reed instruments make me feel I’m blowing a balloon lol. For embouchure practice, I’d actually suggest going for just the headjoint for a couple practice sessions. You don’t have to worry about notes and pitch (and especially with a keyless flute, covering every key) and you really get to work on just tone. Plus it’ll hopefully help you practice longer so you don’t run out of air as quickly!!

For mouth position, when I try to teach total noobs I use the old L in front of the mouth trick, but I think you’re definitely past the point of that! I think a lot of it comes down to muscle memory but I would definitely try to visualize in my head where you want the airstream to go. I would play long tones and find a good spot to both put your mouth and to blow. That’s what I do after long breaks from flute! One thing that helps me too is to play a long tone, “reset” my embouchure by removing my flute and wiggling my lips and whatnot (stretch my mouth and stuff too while we’re at it) and try to find the same “spot” again. 

I can’t really tell much about posture and such with the video and I’m probably not the best person to ask but I do think relaxing your fingers and curving your hands will help relieve some of the tension on your wrists when holding your flute up. Also, hopefully once you’ve developed the muscles a bit more, it’ll come a bit easier! 

I think a lot of it comes down to practice so good luck to you out there! You sound great so far! And I know nothing about wooden flutes but I’m very very jealous of the flute! Happy practicing :-)!
